content: 1. The cumulative number of individuals who have ever started antiretroviral therapy (ART) at a specific facility by the end of the previous reporting period should be recorded. This includes all patients who initiated ART at the facility but excludes those transferred in from other facilities, as they have already been counted in the program elsewhere. 2. During the reporting period, the number of new individuals who started ART at the facility should be tallied. This data can be obtained from the ART register, which organizes patients by the month they began treatment. 3. The cumulative number of individuals who have ever started ART at the facility by the end of the current reporting period should be calculated. This is done by adding the cumulative total from the previous reporting period to the number of new patients who started ART during the current reporting period. 4. The data should be disaggregated by sex and age groups, including males over 14 years, females over 14 years, boys aged 0–14 years, and girls aged 0–14 years. Each individual should be counted in only one category. 5. For antenatal care (ANC), the total number of new ANC clients during the reporting period should be recorded. Among these, the number of women who were known to be HIV-positive at the time of their first ANC visit should be counted. 6. Pregnant women who were not known to be HIV-positive at enrollment in ANC but were tested for HIV and received their results during the reporting period should also be recorded. Among these, the number of women who tested HIV-positive and those who tested HIV-negative should be separately tallied. 7. The total number of pregnant women with known HIV status (both those known to be HIV-positive at arrival and those tested during ANC) should be calculated. Additionally, the total number of HIV-positive pregnant women (including those known at arrival and those newly diagnosed) should be determined. 8. The number of HIV-positive pregnant women who were on ART during the reporting period should be recorded. This includes those who started ART prior to their first ANC visit and those who initiated ART during ANC. 9. For labor and delivery (L&D), the total number of women who delivered at the facility during the reporting period should be recorded. Among these, the number of women with a known HIV-positive status at arrival should be counted. 10. Pregnant women seen in L&D with unknown HIV status who were tested for HIV and received their results during the reporting period should be recorded. Among these, the number of women who tested HIV-positive should be separately tallied. 11. The total number of women with known HIV status in L&D (including those known to be HIV-positive at arrival and those tested during L&D) should be calculated. Additionally, the total number of HIV-positive women in L&D (including those known at arrival and those newly diagnosed) should be determined. 12. The number of HIV-positive women in L&D who were on ART during the reporting period should be recorded. This includes those who started ART during L&D. 13. For HIV-exposed infants, the total number of infants born to HIV-positive mothers within the past 12 months should be recorded. Among these, the number of infants who started antiretroviral (ARV) prophylaxis at birth, received an HIV virological test by two months of age, and started cotrimoxazole (CTX) prophylaxis by two months of age should be separately tallied. 14. The ART register should be used to determine the number of individuals currently on ART at the end of the reporting period. This includes those on first-line, second-line, and third-line ART regimens, disaggregated by age group (adults ≥15 years and children 0–14 years) and sex. 15. The ART regimen recorded for each patient at the end of the reporting period should be used for tallying, even if the patient switched regimens during the reporting period. 16. The total number of adults and children on first-line and second-line regimens should equal the total number of individuals currently on ART. 17. Viral load (VL) suppression data should be recorded for individuals currently on ART. This includes the number of individuals who had a viral load test result recorded in the past 12 months and the number of those with suppressed viral loads during the reporting period. 18. For tuberculosis (TB) treatment, the number of individuals who started TB treatment during the reporting period and were also on ART should be recorded. 19. For syphilis testing and treatment, the number of pregnant women tested for syphilis at their first ANC visit and at any subsequent visit should be recorded. Among those tested, the number who tested positive and the number who received treatment should be separately tallied. 20. The ANC and L&D registers must be reconciled to avoid double-counting women who were already tested and on ART at ANC.
